question.problem:
Rationalize the denominator of the following expression:
$\sqrt{\frac{5}{x+2}}\,=\,$ {{field-1}}
$x+2$
question.worked_solution:
First, we apply the quotient rule and put the numerator and denominator under separate radicals:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{5}{x+2}} & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{x+2}}\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the radical $\sqrt{x+2}$ from the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{x+2}$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{x+2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{x+2}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{x+2}}{\sqrt{x+2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{x+2}}{\sqrt{x+2}\cdot \sqrt{x+2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5(x+2)}}{(\sqrt{x+2})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5(x+2)}}{x+2}\end{aligned}
$$
